title: Measles Is Sickening More Pregnant Women and Newborns, Alarming Doctors
summary: A new analysis underscores the severe consequences of a measles infection during pregnancy, including hospitalization and pregnancy loss.

At least 13 babies have been born infected with measles in the United States in the past two years, as the highly contagious virus has surged across the country, scientists at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported on Monday.


Their preliminary analysis,[published](https://evidence.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/EVIDpha2600416) in the New England Journal of Medicine Evidence, is the first to document how common congenital measles. The authors also identified 112 pregnant women infected with measles in 2025 and 2026, most of whom were unvaccinated. Nearly one-quarter were hospitalized for complications unrelated to labor, such as pneumonia and respiratory failure. One was admitted to the intensive care unit. **** Some also delivered preterm, and two **** lost their pregnancies.


“This is much worse than we thought,” said Michael Osterholm, a public health expert at the University of Minnesota.


Measles is especially dangerous for pregnant women, **** whose immune systems are temporarily weakened. They are more likely to develop severe complications and[10 times as likely to die from measles](https://www.cmaj.ca/content/197/22/E625#:~:text=Pregnant) .


Doctors know relatively little about how being exposed to measles in utero affects children because, until recently, cases of congenital measles were exceedingly rare in the United States. Even before vaccines were available, it was nearly unheard-of for an adult woman to become infected because[almost every American](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/history.html) had measles during childhood.


“There are a lot of holes in our knowledge,” Dr. Adam Ratner, a member of the committee on infectious diseases at the American Academy of Pediatrics, said, adding, “We’ve been lucky enough for the past several decades not to have to think about this.”
